text:
Alex Cheng: Heads-up — I'm seeing a slow-burning IOPS climb on the us-west scratch pool starting ~03:10. Grafana shows sustained small-write churn, not large sequential writes. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/ephemeral-iops?panel=7 :eyes:

Alex Cheng: Quick `df -i` on one impacted node shows inode exhaustion:```
$ df -i /scratch
Filesystem     Inodes  IUsed   IFree IUse% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1 1950720 1950720     0  100% /scratch
```

Tara Nguyen: >/ that is inode exhaustion, not raw disk full. Likely lots of small files (tmp/crash/log fragments). Any recent changes to app temp file usage or the ephemeral-cleaner? :mag:

Petra Kowalski: We did ramp a new batch job last night that writes many tiny checkpoint files to /scratch/tmp, might be the trigger. Cleaner should remove pod-local stuff after termination but there are reports of cleaner loops hitting an eviction race.

Samir Patel: Reproduced locally: when pods are deleted very quickly the kubelet unmounts then the cleaner re-traverses stale mount paths, ends up creating many tiny marker files trying to handle partial deletes -> spiral. I posted a small capture:```
$ sudo find /scratch -xdev -printf '%h
' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 8
120000 /scratch/pods/xyz123/containers/ctr/tmp
30000  /scratch/pods/abc987/containers/ctr/tmp
...
```

Tara Nguyen: We should avoid manual rm -rf across /scratch. Quick mitigation: reduce cleaner concurrency and add an age check before deleting. Can we run a targeted forced cleanup on 4 hot nodes? @ephemeral-cleaner-bot can you run a one-off clean with --dry-run then apply? :pray:

ephemeral-cleaner-bot: scheduled cleanup job started on gnode-234, gnode-237, gnode-241, gnode-251 (mode=force-dryrun).

Alex Cheng: Dryrun reports ~1.6M candidates, mostly under pod tmp and crash directories. If we apply immediately we'll temporarily spike CPU/IO but will free inodes. Downside: cleaner currently spawns 30 deletion workers -> causes heavy metadata IOPS. Suggest lowering to 6 for the force run.

Petra Kowalski: Agree. Also we should throttle GC in kubelet to avoid pod churn while cleaner is running (set eviction threshold to 2% earlier).

Samir Patel: Posted a quick patch in branch infra/cleaner-inode-lock:
- add `--min-age` default 10m
- single leader lock per node to avoid concurrent cleaners
- reduce default worker concurrency to 8
I'll canary that to 10 nodes.

Alex Cheng: For immediate mitigation I'm going to:
1) roll cleaner config to lower concurrency and enable min-age=10m on a subset of nodes (4 nodes)
2) run targeted force-clean (non-dryrun) after hours for the rest of hot nodes
3) schedule a rolling kubelet restart to release lingering mounts where safe

Ira Thompson: Noted. Impact: provisioning stalled for ~3 hours earlier, GPU utilization dipped ~18% in us-west zone because nodes were stuck in cleanup/evict cycle. Ballpark cost impact ~ $2.1k for the window (estimate from cost-dashboard). We'll track in the incident ticket.

Petra Kowalski: One more caveat — fstrim/reclaim will not recover inodes. Only file deletion will. So the fix path is cleaner + reduce pod churn + app patch to write fewer tiny files or batch them.

Tara Nguyen: Quick commands for ops if someone needs them:```
# find top inode-holding dirs under /scratch
sudo find /scratch -xdev -printf '%h
' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 40
# remove only files older than 14d under pod tmp dirs (careful):
sudo find /scratch/pods -type f -mtime +14 -path '*/tmp/*' -delete
```

ephemeral-cleaner-bot: force-clean executed on gnode-234 with concurrency=6; freed ~1,180,000 files, node inode usage dropped to 45%.

Alex Cheng: After canary the cleaner patch and the force-clean we saw node inode usage recover and IOPS normalized. Canary rollout schedule: 10 nodes tonight, 100% by tomorrow morning if no regressions.

Samir Patel: I'll open INFRA-4321 with the postmortem + follow-ups:
- add safer tests for rapid pod delete/create churn
- instrument minute-level inode metrics in Grafana
- add a preflight check to batch jobs that write many small files

Ira Thompson: Thanks team. @oncall - keep an eye on us-west scrub and provisioning queue for the next 12h. We'll do a short postmortem and cost reconciliation tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
